rule: GOAL: Guide the falling piece into a waiting cup by moving the platform beneath it. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the platform left or right; space releases or drops the piece. RULE: The piece lands on the platform only when the platform is directly under it, then can be carried to the cup. TRAP: Do not assume space sends the piece straight into the cup; missing the platform wastes time.

GOAL: The opening puzzle required only one accepted action, not a full arrangement. CONTROLS: Space confirmed the state and cleared the level. RULE: The simplest control can be the whole solution when the visible pieces are a distraction. TRAP: Assuming every block and slot had to be matched before trying the obvious action.

GOAL: Reach the marked exit before the action bar empties. CONTROLS: Arrows: each press is one action and moves up to two cells in that direction. RULE: Unblocked two-cell moves keep the same color; only moves stopped by walls can change it. TRAP: Thinking the exit counts when passed over, not when landed on.

GOAL: Move the piece to the gray square; four clicks were enough. CONTROLS: Click a visible path dot to spend one action and move the piece. RULE: Only dots up to three steps ahead can be clicked; the piece moves to that dot. TRAP: Thinking the blob is the goal or trying dots that are too far wastes time.

GOAL: Use six clicks to set the five marks and run so the piece reaches the goal. CONTROLS: Clicking a part toggles that part; clicking run makes the piece follow the marks. RULE: Each mark's lit parts together choose one move direction, not two separate moves. TRAP: Thinking each lit part adds its own move cost time.

GOAL: set each of five columns to its target shape. CONTROLS: up cycled the current column's item; right moved to the next column. RULE: the level cleared when every column showed the required shape, regardless of pose. TRAP: assuming pose had to match too wasted many actions.

GOAL: Clear the level in six clicks by moving the arrow handle to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Click the arrow to step the boundary; the lower curve moves, and the upper curve shifts opposite. RULE: The boundary is one fixed curve, so moving one side pulls the other side. TRAP: Believing the arrow only changes the lower edge; the linked upper edge opens the path.

The crate only becomes grabbable when you move directly into it; sliding under it from the side does not count. A clean 10-action route is: Left 3, Down, Up, Space, Right 3, Space. The Down/Up step is what makes it contact the crate from below. Then Space absorbs it, and Space drops it after carrying it right.

GOAL: Reach the gate in four clicks by aligning the block. CONTROLS: Each click moves two linked boundaries in opposite directions; the block follows one. RULE: Linked boundaries keep a fixed total, so only some alignments can match the gate. TRAP: Assuming the block moves freely; hidden linked boundaries can block apparent positions.

GOAL: place the bars so three rising pieces enter the three top notches. CONTROLS: arrows moved the selected bar, mouse changed the selected bar, space ran the puzzle. RULE: a piece rises until the first bar blocks it, so lower bars decide its split. TRAP: thinking a top gap was enough; a lower bar could stop it first.

GOAL: Clear the level in two clicks by moving a piece so it merges with another near the target. CONTROLS: A click could create a piece at an empty spot or move a chosen piece toward the click. RULE: The merged piece appears at the moving piece's landing point, not at the midpoint or the other piece. TRAP: Thinking the other piece would move or that any merge point was acceptable; the landing point decided the result.

GOAL: Set every slot to the right shape kind, not the exact drawing shown. CONTROLS: Arrows: some arrows moved slots, others changed the chosen shape. RULE: The check accepted any turn or flip of the right shape kind. TRAP: I lost time trying to match the pose instead of the kind.

GOAL: This level required arranging blocks into slots so the target row matched, using the check to learn the order. CONTROLS: Click to pick a block, click to place or swap it, space to test. RULE: The check flashes the first wrong target and the slot that failed; the order is hidden. TRAP: Do not assume each target sits above the slot it controls; use the flash to find the rule.

GOAL: This level required placing pieces so a hidden path collected them in the right order. CONTROLS: Clicking a piece selects it, clicking a slot places it, and space tests the board. RULE: A box always starts at its leftmost slot, and a portal path is followed fully before returning. TRAP: Believing the pipe entry sets the order inside a box cost time; it does not.

GOAL: Cross the room to the exit in three arrow moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one space. RULE: The guard only reacts along its row, and stepping into its cell is safe. TRAP: Do not assume the guard’s cell is deadly; avoiding it can make the path impossible.

ESTABLISHED: The tip can change size; lighting four grid cells triggers a check. FAILED: Clicking panel blocks, handle, or tip did nothing; the blue tip failed the check and shrank. GOAL IS NOT: simply lighting four cells with the current tip. CONTROLS: Clicks toggle grid cells; the fourth click starts a check; UP and DOWN rotate the tip; panel clicks did nothing.

GOAL: Fill all slots so the traversal order, including the portal detour, matches the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click a piece then a slot to place it; press space to submit or clear. RULE: The portal’s slot inserts the connected box’s items into the main order at that point. TRAP: Assuming the portal can be placed last; its position decides which fixed piece must match which target.

GOAL: Set the bars to the heights that make the blocks line up. CONTROLS: Each button shifts height between two adjacent bars, lowering one and raising the other. RULE: A bar stops rising when it reaches the space allowed by the block or edge above it. TRAP: Do not assume a bar can always rise to the needed height; its cap may force you to move other bars first.

GOAL: Place blocks and portals so the red and blue boxes expose the target color sequence. CONTROLS: Click a palette block to pick it, click a slot to place it, press space to submit. RULE: Each portal pair links the blue box to the red slots it covers, so the blue triple must match that segment. TRAP: Assuming the blue box shows the first three target slots instead of the portal-linked segment.

GOAL: Fill each linked box so its three pieces match the target triplets. CONTROLS: Click to pick and place pieces or portals; space checks and clears. RULE: The first target piece identifies the box; put the matching portal in the red box, then fill that linked box. TRAP: Thinking any portal fits any red slot; a wrong portal sends you to the wrong box.

ESTABLISHED: The level is not cleared; only blocks covered by the beam move when it moves, left/right movement packs blocks, and blocks on a row cannot pass each other. FAILED: Trying to create space by pushing blocks together on a row did nothing; their order stayed fixed. GOAL IS NOT: Packing the blocks tightly or placing them side by side. CONTROLS: Up and down move the beam and drag covered blocks; left and right move it and push blocks on its row.

GOAL: Send the plug straight up into the socket without overlap. CONTROLS: Clicking the left marks changes the command; clicking run applies it. RULE: The card that produces upward motion is correct, even if a flip flicker appears. TRAP: Thinking the flicker means the plug must be upside down.

GOAL: Arrange colors and portals so the linked boxes read as one target sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette, click slots, press space to test. RULE: A portal inserts its matching box in place, so nested boxes can count. TRAP: Believing portals must stay in the outer box; nesting is required.

GOAL: Remove the guards, then reach the goal. CONTROLS: Each arrow key moved the player one step in its direction. RULE: A guard’s eyes show its facing, and it only lunges straight ahead when close. TRAP: Thinking any guard in the same line was dangerous; only a close guard facing you mattered.

GOAL: Clear the level in nine clicks by moving the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Click a glyph to erase it, click a card to preview the ghost move, and click the blue button to submit. RULE: The plain stem meant one direction; adding the bar changed it, so test one small edit at a time. TRAP: Thinking every column had to be edited before testing; one preview revealed the real move and saved clicks.

GOAL: Set the blue slots to the decoded target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; up and down cycled the slot under it. RULE: The yellow strip was segmented dotted words, each translating to solid letters. TRAP: Thinking exact poses or full cycle probing was required cost time.

GOAL: Convert the solid blue question glyphs into the dotted yellow answer glyphs. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active glyph and committed the chosen match. RULE: Follow the two step chain: blue solid to pink solid, then pink solid to yellow dotted. TRAP: Assuming blue and yellow are paired directly instead of using the pink step.

GOAL: The level needed the piece to collect the target dots, not to solve a hidden switch. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; the special key only changed control and was not needed. RULE: The level completed when all required marks were touched, so simple movement exposed the real objective. TRAP: Believing the bright yellow cross or an extra key was required wasted time.

GOAL: Move the yellow block into the bracket in five clicks. CONTROLS: Red rotates the ring one way, green rotates it the other way. RULE: The bracket marks the target, and each click shifts the ring one place. TRAP: The side arrows are controls, not exits, and the top marks are not the goal.

GOAL: Make each moving part reach the marked target by changing its length the correct number of times. CONTROLS: Click one button to grow a part and the other to shrink it, watching how far each click moves it. RULE: The length changes in fixed jumps, so only certain lengths can ever reach the target; find the jump before clicking. TRAP: I wasted time assuming any length was possible, then probing randomly instead of solving for a reachable length.

GOAL: Clear the level in five clicks by getting the active piece to the goal. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece, then click again to move it to a valid spot. RULE: Only clicks on the actual piece or a legal empty spot change the board. TRAP: Assuming a visible ring is a finished move wastes time; it may be only a cue.

GOAL: Clear the level in seven arrow moves by reaching the plus and matching the box. CONTROLS: Up, down, left, right arrows moved the piece one step; the plus changed the symbol when reached. RULE: The symbol changes only on the plus, so the final move must land there. TRAP: Assuming the symbol updates after every move or that the piece itself rotates.

GOAL: Make the lower right panel's center red to clear the level. CONTROLS: A click toggles a cell; clicking the center turns the mini into a red block. RULE: The center mini was the cell to change, not a preview of the panel. TRAP: Thinking the mini was locked or only a guide.

GOAL: Make the panel match the small preview patterns by coloring the right cells. CONTROLS: Click a panel cell to change its color; previews only show the goal. RULE: Each preview is a zoomed target for the panel area around it. TRAP: Thinking the preview itself must be clicked wastes time; match only the panel.

GOAL: Clear it in two clicks by placing the square on the ring. CONTROLS: Click the diamond to swap the two ends; click a valid spot to move the white end. RULE: The square sits halfway between the two ends, so one end must be opposite the ring from the other. TRAP: Thinking the white end must reach the ring; swap first if that makes the halfway point land on it.

GOAL: Move each yellow block into a bracket. CONTROLS: Click row arrows to shift a row; click ring arrows to rotate the ring. RULE: Row and ring cross at shared cells, so either move can carry a block into place. TRAP: Assuming a move only affects its own row or ring, not the crossing cell, cost time.

GOAL: Make the needed grid cells match the colors shown by the mini displays. CONTROLS: Clicking cells changed their color; mini displays were fixed hints. RULE: Each mini shows the target pattern for its area, and shared cells must agree. TRAP: Believing the mini displays are clickable or separate puzzles wasted moves.

GOAL: The level required placing both target tokens on their marked spots. CONTROLS: Left forward/back rotated the left ring one step; right forward/back did the same on the right. RULE: Shared spots transferred tokens between rings, so one rotation could move a token onto the other ring. TRAP: Believing the rings were independent caused wasted moves.

GOAL: Cover every scattered dot with the moving cross. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cross; Space switched it between a diagonal cross and a straight cross. RULE: A dot counts only when a cross arm rests on it, and moving away uncovers it again. TRAP: Mistaking uncovered dots for new or recolored dots, instead of seeing them as old dots revealed by the cross moving.

ESTABLISHED: This level is not cleared; frames show two identical blocks in separate colored areas moving as mirrored pairs. FAILED: A long one-block route and treating the changing bar as a step count did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: It is not a single-block path, not a bar timer, and not a simple pass-through swap. CONTROLS: Left, right, up, and down moved one block; the other block made the opposite move.

GOAL: Clear the first room by letting a recorded copy hold the plate while you finish the route. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space records the path and sends the copy along it. RULE: The copy repeats the saved moves, so it can keep a pressure plate down for you. TRAP: The replay does not start exactly when your first move began; assume its timing is delayed.

GOAL: guide the marked tip of a moving shape to its target. CONTROLS: clicking a color's control extends or retracts that color. RULE: the whole shape must clear obstacles while moving, not only the tip. TRAP: trusting that a clear tip means a safe move; the body can collide.

GOAL: Rotate the carried symbol to the shown pattern, then bring it to its matching place before the bar empties. CONTROLS: Arrows move; a blocked move bounces and rotates the symbol, and each press spends bar. RULE: The bar drains every action and refills at safe spots, so keep a margin. TRAP: Assuming the shown symbol was already correct; it needed one more turn.

GOAL: fit the two blocks into the single shared gap. CONTROLS: arrows moved both blocks at once; two presses solved it. RULE: every block shifted together, so the gap was the clear target. TRAP: thinking the blocks needed separate routes or hidden keys.

Understood. Level 4 is cleared with only three clicks, so the intended solution is the minimal one: select the three mini elements/centers directly. The longer panel-repainting inference was unnecessary; once those three required targets are activated, the level completes.

ESTABLISHED: The level is still unsolved after exceeding its normal move budget; the left area is open for the player, and the right block is separate. FAILED: Player-only wandering and trying to reach the socket did not clear it. GOAL IS NOT: Simply standing in the visible socket, or expecting the block to slide into it from the left. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player; no tested control affected the separate block.

GOAL: Move the marked pieces to their matching bracket slots. CONTROLS: Left and right rotate the horizontal loop; up and down rotate the vertical loop. RULE: Each move shifts every piece on the chosen loop one step, with the end wrapping to the start. TRAP: Do not assume the two loops are independent; they share corner cells, so one move changes both.

GOAL: Put the block with the white dot into the waiting socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block under the white dot; clicking a block moves the white dot onto it. RULE: The white dot marks the block you can steer. TRAP: Assuming the block you clicked or the dark-dotted block is the one arrows control.

GOAL: clear the board by clicking the true centers of the hidden diamonds in six actions. CONTROLS: a click selected a candidate center and confirmed it. RULE: the center is the diamond’s own central pixel, not the first edge point or a guessed offset. TRAP: assuming edge order always reveals the center wasted time when shapes overlapped or were partly covered.

GOAL: Move the two blocks safely to their goals using arrow moves. CONTROLS: Each arrow slides both blocks one step; a block stopped by a wall does not move. RULE: Hazards are deadly floor, not walls: if either block would enter one, the level fails. TRAP: Assuming a hazard would block a slide like a wall; it instead kills the block and resets.

GOAL: insert the plug into the socket so its tips cover the matching contacts. CONTROLS: arrows shifted the plug, space turned it, and each press spent time. RULE: arrows moved the plug by fixed jumps, so counting jumps solved the fit. TRAP: thinking the plug had to be turned when only arrow jumps were needed.

GOAL: Get the dark piece to the yellow target in two arrow presses. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the dotted piece; the solid piece mirrored it. RULE: Across the divider, left and right reversed, while up and down matched. TRAP: Believing the solid piece moves the way you press wastes moves.

GOAL: Fill the canvas to match the reference by painting the required color areas. CONTROLS: Click a color to load the tool. Space paints from the tool. RULE: The reference shows the finished areas; the tool must hold that color before painting. TRAP: Thinking a click alone changes the canvas; it only selects, so space is still needed.

GOAL: Guide the player through the rotating arm to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move; clicks press buttons to rotate parts or open gates. RULE: Mechanisms change what is passable, so test them before committing to a path. TRAP: Do not assume gray or red blocks are walls; some are rooms you can enter.

GOAL: set the sequence of moves needed for the object to reach the goal. CONTROLS: click a mark to toggle it; press run to apply the sequence. RULE: each column’s mark pattern becomes one move, and a blank column does nothing. TRAP: assuming previous test clicks left the marks as you thought; toggles may have undone them.

GOAL: Cover the target using ten arrow moves while keeping the reflection legal. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; space switched movement modes. RULE: The level cleared when the piece exactly covered the target. TRAP: Assuming arrow directions stayed the same in both modes cost time.

GOAL: make a two-color pattern: one color on the top band, another on the lower diagonal corner. CONTROLS: arrows move the nozzle, swatches pick the paint, space applies the current paint shape. RULE: each nozzle position paints a whole region, so match the target by covering regions, not tiny pieces. TRAP: assuming many actions are needed when the starting nozzle and color already solve it with one action.

ESTABLISHED: The bubble moves horizontally, rises through blue openings, and cannot cross black barriers; the upper blue area is reachable only through a left gap. FAILED: Moving the bubble left into that gap did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Not simply reaching the upper blue area, and not filling every black cell. CONTROLS: LEFT shifts the bubble left; no other control effect is known.

GOAL: The level wanted a tight route for paired pieces, solved in four clicks. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a destination to move it. RULE: Moves succeed when the middle point fits, even if the pieces overlap others. TRAP: Assuming solved pieces block the corridor; the middle point can slip past them.

GOAL: Put the two yellow blocks into the bracketed end slots. CONTROLS: Red arrows rotate a row or the winding track; green arrows run that move backward. RULE: The row and track share slots, so each click shifts a whole loop and the order of clicks matters. TRAP: Thinking one block can be moved alone; every move carries several blocks and can undo your work.

GOAL: Raise the bubble to the room’s highest point. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move it; one arrow action cleared the level. RULE: A new highest position advances the screen. TRAP: Do not assume the pink marker is the goal.

GOAL: cover every marked point with the moving shape. CONTROLS: arrow keys slide the current shape; space cycles it to the next shape. RULE: a point is covered only when a shape arm passes through it, and the cycle order is fixed. TRAP: assuming space picks any shape directly; it only advances one step, so plan switches early.

GOAL: Finish the level by using one trigger instead of a long route. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece one step; touching a trigger sent it away. RULE: A trigger always sent the piece away from itself, not from your entry direction. TRAP: Thinking the launch direction depended on how you entered cost time.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving every diamond to its required place within the action limit. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to make it active, then click an empty spot to move it there. RULE: The diamond you just moved stays active, so repeated moves from it cost only one click each. TRAP: Believing each move needs a new activation click, which wastes actions when the last-moved diamond is already active.

GOAL: Put each marked block into the bracketed slot. CONTROLS: Turn moved a block one spoke; Ring moved it one ring; Center swapped the three paired slots. RULE: Spoke and ring moves wrapped around, so count the steps instead of guessing. TRAP: Thinking you could rotate the shorter way; the turn control only moved one direction.

GOAL: Reproduce the target pattern by loading colors and firing the nozzle from the matching sides. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the nozzle, clicking a swatch loads paint, Space fires, and clicking a cap uses it. RULE: Each firing position paints a simple band of cells, so the target tells you which position and color to use. TRAP: Thinking a cap is missing because it is not visible; it can appear only after the right color is loaded.

GOAL: Rotate the linked shapes until their looped pieces line up. CONTROLS: Clicking red or green arrows turned the whole connected loop one step; the two colors were opposite directions. RULE: Each arrow showed the rotation direction of the loop it touched, not a single cell. TRAP: Thinking arrows pointed to a destination instead of the way the entire shape turns.

GOAL: Cover all marked spots with the shapes at once, matching the needed colors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the chosen shape; space switches to the other shape. RULE: A shape keeps the color of the last square it touched, even after leaving it. TRAP: Thinking a shape reverts to its old color when it leaves the colored square.

ESTABLISHED: Frames show a colored grid, clickable cells, small figures, glyphs, and color clues; purple, green, and magenta appear. FAILED: Guessing glyph values, reading glyphs as nearby color counts, and probing covered cells for hidden colors did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: literal glyph matching, count matching, or a rule to carry to the new game. CONTROLS: Clicking cells changes or cycles their color; no other control was observed to affect the puzzle.

GOAL: match the target by loading colors and applying them where each tool points. CONTROLS: click a swatch to load a color, space to spray from the nozzle, click the cap to deposit its loaded color. RULE: the active tool uses the color you last selected, and it changes only its own area. TRAP: I assumed the cap frame was clickable; only its active center accepted the deposit.

GOAL: Paint the target pattern with a few moves, color choices, and sprays. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the nozzle, clicks chose a color, space painted. RULE: Directional strokes cover bracket-shaped areas; diagonal strokes include their diagonal line. TRAP: Thinking a diagonal stroke leaves the diagonal line unpainted cost time.

GOAL: move the player onto the target plate. CONTROLS: arrows moved the player; clicking a button rotated that color’s bar. RULE: the player could only pass matching color paths, so choose or change a path before entering it. TRAP: assuming a bar stays as seen; a button press can open one path and block another.

GOAL: Carry the block to the gate by lifting it on the right pool. CONTROLS: Bars moved white between adjacent pools; the door shifted the block sideways. RULE: The door opens only when the block is aligned with its window and the receiving surface is low enough. TRAP: Raising the receiving pool too early keeps the door shut and wastes moves.

GOAL: Reach the goal while the legend shows the required color and shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece; it slides until blocked, and special tiles trigger. RULE: A color circle changes the legend when touched; stepping off and back cycles it. TRAP: Do not assume one touch gives the target color; test the legend after each cycle.

GOAL: Get to the goal while a recorded self replays and presses switches. CONTROLS: Arrows move; space begins the replay; a blocked arrow still advances time. RULE: The replay moves one step per real turn, so arrive just after the switch is pressed. TRAP: Thinking a blocked arrow is harmless waiting; it can lock your next action.

GOAL: Put the square on the ring by placing the diamonds so their average is the ring. CONTROLS: Click a diamond to choose it, then click a clear spot to move it; each diamond moves once. RULE: The square follows the average center of the diamonds after every move, and that spot must be clear. TRAP: Putting a diamond on the ring center; it blocks the square's final space.

GOAL: Finish within the action limit by using recorded runs to hold switches open. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved; Space ended a recorded run and replayed it. RULE: Recorded runs repeat exactly, so past moves can keep gates clear for the live run. TRAP: Assuming the action meter counted every key; it counted only live arrow moves.

GOAL: Cover the marked cells with the object and its reflected copies. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; Space switched the selection. RULE: Each mirror flipped the object across its line, and the pair created the opposite image. TRAP: Believing the reflections had to fit exactly; extra cover was allowed.

GOAL: Park every dot in a dead-end spot, then merge them with the blocks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected object; clicks choose a dot or activate blocks. RULE: Only the object you just clicked responds to arrows, so select before moving. TRAP: Thinking a parked dot stays active; that wastes moves and forces extra clicks.

GOAL: Move the block to the far band by shaping widths and opening the correct door. CONTROLS: A bar's up or down control shifts width between the two bands it separates; clicking a door moves a block through it. RULE: A door opens, and changes color, only when the two bands beside it have equal width. TRAP: Believing a band can absorb unlimited width wastes moves; changes stop at its limit.

GOAL: reach the goal by opening the right path. CONTROLS: arrows move the player; clicking the bar rotates it. RULE: the bar’s direction connects or blocks the nearby gates. TRAP: assuming the gate was useless while the bar was horizontal; it had to be turned first.

GOAL: Move the mirror into place, then use space and an arrow. CONTROLS: Space did the action, arrows moved the mirror. RULE: Only actions that change the board are trusted. TRAP: Thinking a blank action is safe in a group cost time.

ESTABLISHED: Stopping under a black ceiling advances the screen; stopping under purple kills. FAILED: Popping the block above the bubble and moving left did nothing useful; it stays trapped or dies. GOAL IS NOT: The nearest hole or clearing all blocks. CONTROLS: Pop removes a block; Left nudges the bubble; rising is automatic.

GOAL: Move the block to the gate by shifting white space and passing through open doors. CONTROLS: The lane buttons moved white space between lanes; the lit doors moved the block up or down. RULE: A door opened when the block sat in its window, touching the white edge. TRAP: Thinking the door depended only on total white width; it depended on the block’s exact place.

ESTABLISHED: all launchers emptied, blocks were split by bars, and pieces landed in notches. FAILED: clearing by using every block and filling every notch did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: only filling notches, emptying launchers, or using all blocks. CONTROLS: launch actions fired blocks, bars altered their paths, and notch cups received pieces.

ESTABLISHED: Boxes can be moved into crate spaces, and the orange figure also moves boxes. FAILED: Filling only part of the crate did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Just filling part of the crate. CONTROLS: Up, down, left, and right move; space grabs or drops a held box.

GOAL: Get both pieces to the same goal without getting trapped by gates. CONTROLS: Up, down, left, and right moved both pieces together. RULE: A switch opened gates only while a piece stood on it. TRAP: Thinking a long careful plan was safer than testing a short arrow move.

GOAL: Clear the level by making the real check pass, not by copying the white guide pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved or turned the active piece; four presses solved it, and each press counted as one action.
